jobs.conversationalHeadline: This idea survived the calculations, but it still needs a real-world experiment.
jobs.plainEnglishSummary: We investigated why solid-state batteries short-circuit even when protected by super-hard ceramic glass. Using magma dike hydraulics from geology, we proved that charging overpotentials create explosive internal pressures over 740 MPa (7,300 atmospheres) inside micro-notches, easily exceeding the ceramic fracture limit. When we tried to prove this wrong, we found lithium can creep out of surface cracks—which led us to bring in semiconductor physics: tiny electrical leaks allow lithium to grow inside sealed pores deep within the ceramic with nowhere to escape.
jobs.sharedMechanism: Confined fluid/solid phase transformation under thermodynamic overpotential: electrochemical potential transforms directly into hydrostatic tensile stress (P = -eta * F / Vm) concentrated at flaw tips, overcoming bulk compressive resistance.
jobs.unaskedQuestionDiscovered: Instead of asking "How can we make solid electrolytes harder or polish their surfaces smoother?", the unasked question is: "How do we reduce the electronic leakage of ceramic grain boundaries below 10^-10 S/cm so electrons cannot nucleate lithium inside sealed internal pores?"
jobs.contradictionOrClash: Classical battery engineering insisted mechanical stiffness prevents dendrites. Fracture mechanics proved stiffness is irrelevant if pressure builds up inside flaws; semiconductor physics proved electronic leakage—not mechanical softness—is the root culprit.
conditionsWhereItWorks: Fast-charging solid-state lithium metal batteries with polycrystalline ceramic electrolytes (such as LLZO, LATP, and sulfide glasses).
High current density charging (J > 1.0 mA/cm2) and low operating temperatures (< 25 deg C) where lithium plastic creep is too slow to relieve stress.
conditionsWhereItFails: Liquid electrolyte batteries with flexible porous polymer separators.
Single-crystal ceramic electrolytes with zero grain boundaries and zero internal micro-porosity.
Elevated operating temperatures (> 60 deg C) where lithium yield stress drops below 0.3 MPa, allowing rapid plastic stress relaxation.
